# What AWS Quick Is and Who It's For: An AI Workspace Built for Work

> **In short:** Amazon Web Services (AWS) has launched AWS Quick, an AI workspace built only for work. According to AWS, teams can use AI agents to research and analyze the data and apps they already use, and it has no consumer version.

If you have ever bounced between a CRM, a spreadsheet, your email, and a dashboard just to prepare one client update, you know how much time that takes. AWS says its new tool, AWS Quick, is meant to pull those pieces together in one place.

## What AWS Quick is

AWS Quick is an AI workspace, which means a shared place where you and your coworkers work with an AI assistant. The company describes it as built for work from the start, not adapted from a consumer app.

The key idea is the **AI agent**. An agent (a program that can carry out a task for you, not just answer a question) can look up information, compare it, and take the next step. AWS says Quick works across the applications and workflows your team already uses, so it can understand how your projects, people, and data connect.

AWS also says that anyone can build simple agents, apps, and automations by describing what they need in plain language. You do not have to file an IT ticket first. Anything built in a shared space can be used by the whole team.

## Why AWS says the security matters

Many office AI tools raise a fair question: where does my company's data go? AWS says Quick connects to the security tools organizations already use, such as Microsoft Purview (a tool for protecting data) and Microsoft Active Directory (a system that controls who can access what).

Here are a few of the safeguards AWS describes:

- **Permissions stay in force.** Quick reads the sensitivity labels already on your files (tags that mark how private a document is) and respects existing access rules.
- **Approved sharing.** Agents, knowledge bases (collections of documents the AI can search), and skills reach new teams only through approval, and each decision is recorded.
- **An audit trail.** An audit trail is a log showing what happened, who did it, and when. AWS says this is built in.
- **Certifications.** AWS says Quick carries compliance certifications, including HIPAA, FedRAMP, SOC 2, and ISO 27001. Each is a formal standard that auditors check against.

AWS also says your conversations are private, IT admins cannot read chat transcripts, and your data never trains someone else's models.

## Companies using it

AWS names 3M, BMW, Mondelez, New York Life, and Southwest Airlines as enterprises using Quick. The company is also launching its first brand campaign in the United States and the United Kingdom.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: Quick is aimed at workplaces, so most people will meet it through their employer rather than on their own.
- **For your business or work**: If your organization is considering it, bring your IT and security teams in early. AWS says permissions and audit logs are built in, but your company still decides who gets access.
- **If you're just getting started**: Ask your manager or IT team whether Quick is available to you, and what rules apply to using it with company files. For pricing and enterprise options, check AWS's official pricing page or talk to your AWS account team.
- **If you already use it**: Once you are comfortable, try building a small, shared agent for a repeating task, such as preparing a weekly summary. Then ask your admin whether it can be approved for the rest of your team, and check the audit trail to confirm who has access.

## Wrap-up

AWS Quick is a work-only AI workspace where agents can research and act across your company's existing data and apps, with security and audit tools that AWS says are built in. Its main promise is saving time on repetitive work while keeping control with your organization. Your next step is simple: find out whether your company uses Quick, and ask one question about how your team's files are protected before you start.
